title: Double Speed? Connected Bodies Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
An engine pulls coaches, a lift rides with a counterweight, a flag climbs its pole on a rope. Tied bodies move as one. Aarav ties a small bag to a toy trolley over a pulley at the edge of his study table, then doubles the bag. Does the trolley go twice as fast? No. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we solve connected bodies and pulley systems.

On a live motion notebook an Atwood machine runs with 3 and 3, 5 and 3, then 9 and 3 kilograms, with a live readout of a, T and v and a graph of acceleration against the mass ratio that climbs towards g but never reaches it. A slow-mo replay gives each block its own free-body diagram. Then the rule step by step (a = (m1 - m2)g/(m1 + m2), T = 2m1m2g/(m1 + m2)), why T sits between the two weights, the bag and trolley (a = m2 g/(m1 + m2)), two blocks pulled from either end (a = F/(m1 + m2)), two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with three coaches, the exam trap about the force on a pulley, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
